title: Token causality attribution pipeline and adaptive trace sampling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a production pipeline that attaches causal metadata to token-level events so downstream billing, latency SLOs, and cache-economics dashboards can reconcile per-token costs. This ticket covers: 1) a light-weight trace hook that records token lifecycle events (emit, kv_lookup, kv_miss, kernel_execute, token_sent) with causality links; 2) an adaptive sampling policy that guarantees 100% sampling for high-cost/error flows and probabilistic sampling elsewhere; 3) an ingestion path that enriches events with model, route, quantization profile, and runtime kernel tags; 4) ETL rules to compute cache delta attribution and per-token latency breakdowns in ClickHouse/BigQuery for dashboards and billing reports. Non-goals: rewriting existing token probes in every runtime; per-customer billing exports (handled by a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
- Trace hooks can emit token-level events with stable schema (schema v1) and unique causality ids.
- Adaptive sampler exposes config flags and default policy in yaml.
- Ingested events produce token-level latency-series and cache-hit offset metrics in staging dashboards.
- End-to-end test reproduces a synthetic prefix-cache hit/miss workload and shows correct attribution in dashboard panels and billing reconciliation job.
- Documentation and SDK hooks added to the runtime README and internal Confluence page.
implementation_notes: Architecture: add TraceTokenEvent struct to runtime with fields: causality_id, token_index, phase, ts_ns, kv_key_hash (opaque), cache_hit boolean, kernel_id, seq_len, model_variant, route_id. Events are emitted synchronously for sampled requests and buffered to a per-worker ring for async flush to an agent via gRPC. Sampling: introduce an adaptive sampler module supporting deterministic sampling by route + quantile thresholds for runtime latency and a hard rule to always sample any request with error codes >=500 or cache-miss ratio >0.6. Ingestion: a lightweight collector will validate schema, apply enrichment rules (model catalog lookup, quantization profile), and forward to batching Kafka topic. ETL: a ClickHouse materialized view computes token-level latency components and attribute per-token chargebacks using rules from the Optimize team. Backwards compatibility: payloads include an event_version field for future extension.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for event serialization and sampler thresholds.
- Integration test: run runtime with a synthetic workload that alternates prefix reuse to exercise cache hits/misses; assert per-token cache_hit counts match internal counters.
- Load test: ensure event emission adds <1% p99 latency overhead at expected QPS (run with dedicated capacity in staging).
- Regression: run existing billing reconciliation on sample dataset to compare totals before/after; delta should be explainable by newly attributed cache-chargebacks.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy to canary hosts (5% traffic) with sampling disabled by default. 2) Enable sampling at low-rate (0.5%) and monitor ingestion and disk/network overhead. 3) Ramp sampling for error/high-cost flows only. 4) Once stable, enable full sampling for debugging buckets and activate ETL jobs for staging dashboards. 5) Graduate to runtime-1.20 GA with default sampler policy. Rollback: flip feature flag and purge collector buffers.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry volume explosion -> Mitigation: adaptive sampler defaults to strict limits and maximum events per-request cap.
- Risk: PII leakage via token payloads -> Mitigation: only emit token hashes and indices; never raw token text; collector runs a schema validator that rejects plaintext.
- Risk: increased request latency -> Mitigation: non-blocking buffered emission path and backpressure safeguards to drop telemetry when output queue exceeds thresholds.
- Risk: attribution disagreements with legacy billing -> Mitigation: run reconciliation job in dry-run and provide a diff dashboard for 2 weeks before switching billing pipeline.
